What's new in Callout 0.7.7

Version 0.7.7 Alpha

0.7.7 adds one control, asked for by several of you in different words: the size of the image that leaves Callout. Click the pill at the bottom (or right-click it, as before) and under the formats you will find 100%, 75%, 50% and 25%, each showing the pixel size it makes, plus Custom… — a slider whose percentage and pixel size follow your hand — and Reset to 100%. It applies to everything that leaves — the pill drag, ⌘C, Export…, and the Library’s export — and never to the Card itself, which keeps every pixel. On a Retina Mac, 50% is exactly the size the capture had on screen, which is what a chat window expects.

It stays set until you change it, and you can always see it: at 100% the pill looks as it always has; at anything else it reads the format and the percent, the copy confirmation names the size that left, and the export panel shows it too. Nothing is ever scaled up.

New

  • Choose the size of what leaves. Click the pill for the format and the scale. Sticky, global, always visible when it is not 100%. Rendered at the chosen size rather than shrunk afterwards, so arrows and text stay crisp and only the picture is resampled.

What's new in Callout 0.7.6

Version 0.7.6 Alpha

0.7.6 is housekeeping with one thing you will notice. Press Esc to cancel a capture and you stay in the app you were in — Callout no longer comes forward on a cancel, just as it never comes forward on the way in. Under the hood, the tool cursors rebuild themselves when you switch between light and dark, and the shipped app no longer carries a path from the build machine in its library search list.

Nothing else changed. If you are reading this in the update window, that is the point: small fixes arrive as soon as they exist.

Fixed

  • Esc leaves you where you were. Cancel a capture and the app you were in stays in front. Callout used to come forward on every exit, cancel included, because the alerts that explain a failed capture share that exit and need it. Now only those alerts bring it forward — and a new Card still opens Callout as before.
  • Housekeeping. Tool cursors rebuild on a light/dark switch; the packaged app carries no build-machine paths; the app builds with no compiler warnings, so the next one will be seen.

What's new in Callout 0.7.5

Version 0.7.5 Alpha

0.7.5 does one thing: the crosshair now appears only while you are selecting a region to capture. After the capture, over the Card, the pointer is the ordinary arrow with the tool’s badge riding on it — not a crosshair. Since August every drawing tool had put its badge on a crosshair, so the moment a Card landed under the pointer the crosshair was back; with the capture crosshair lost and found twice in 0.7.4, that became impossible to unsee. The text tool keeps its I-beam, and hovering anything you drew still shows the hand.

Nothing else changed. If you are reading this in the update window, that is the point: small fixes arrive as soon as they exist.

Fixed

  • The crosshair belongs to capture. It is the pointer while you drag out a region, and nowhere else. On the Card the tool badge now rides on the arrow, exactly where it always sat, so where a click lands does not move.
